summary: Sections that collapse, with the document's heading structure intact. Holds the open set and the heading level.
useWhen: a page has several long sections and most users need one of them
optional or advanced settings should be present but not in the way
an FAQ or a reference list where scanning titles is the primary action

useInstead.when: the sections are alternatives and only one is ever relevant
useInstead.why: tabs say "pick one"; an accordion says "all of these exist, open what you need"

useInstead.when: hiding the content would hide something the user must act on
useInstead.why: a required field inside a collapsed section is a form that cannot be completed without exploration

requires: `headingLevel` that fits the surrounding document — the default of 3 is a guess this component cannot verify
notes: each section's trigger is a button inside a heading, which is the only arrangement that keeps both document structure and operability
collapsed panels are hidden rather than unmounted, so form state survives and in-page search still finds the text

antiPatterns.do: leave it off, so opening one section closes the last
antiPatterns.why: with every section openable at once the page has no maximum height, and a user who opens six is scrolling a wall of text looking for the one they wanted. Reach for it when sections are settings or reference material a user may need to compare side by side

antiPatterns.dont: headingLevel left at 3 inside a section already under an h4
antiPatterns.why: the page looks correct and its outline is nonsense — a heading-level jump is invisible to sighted users and disorienting to everyone navigating by headings

antiPatterns.dont: an accordion holding a single section
antiPatterns.why: one collapsible section is a control that exists to hide the only thing on screen
